Taylor: FYI starting canary bring-up for halberd18b-int4 on dedicated, seeing sporadic OOMs during steady traffic, can someone look?
Ash: how often and on which fleet?
Taylor: per-instance across canary pool. Canary run 1 showed 2 OOMs in ~12m. Workload is multi-turn chat, avg input ~350 tokens.
Ash: paste the OOM log if you have it
Taylor: ```
[2026-03-22T15:12:04Z] ERROR oom: alloc failed at kv_cache_grow
model=halberd18b-int4 pool=gpu0
config: batch_size=4, window=12, max_new_tokens=1024, prefetch=true, slot_reserve=0.05
trace: alloc 3.2GB -> failed
```
infra-bot: canary-run-id=cr-20260322-halb-1 status=failed events=2 runtime-version=0.14.0
Mira: int4 + large max_new_tokens is a common frag combo. 1024 is aggressive for this family.
Kevin: on similar 18b-family models we capped batch_size=2 during warmup and set max_new_tokens default to 512. Also bumped slot_reserve to 0.12 for int4.
Taylor: did a micro-benchmark vs int8 on a 50-prompt sample: int8 p50=210ms tokens/s=280, int4 p50=230ms tokens/s=300. Quick auto-eval (100 prompts) showed ~-1.8% rouge-L for int4.
Ash: so int4 is slightly faster/costly but has a small quality hit and frag risk.
Mira: options: lower default max_new_tokens, raise slot_reserve, enable soft-evict/k-v trim heuristics, or use mixed-precision fallback for critical routes.
Kevin: runtime 0.14.0 lacks the slab compaction/soft-evict fixes we shipped in 0.14.2. Does the canary use that older runtime?
infra-bot: runtime-version=0.14.0 for cr-20260322-halb-1
Ash: plan: upgrade canary runtime to 0.14.2, and test config: max_new_tokens=512, batch_size=2, slot_reserve=0.12, session_cache=false, kv_trim_threshold=0.6. Add OOM alert.
Taylor: repro curl I used:
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD" \
 -d '{"model":"halberd18b-int4","input":"<conv>","max_new_tokens":1024,"batch_size":4}'
```
Kevin: also try disabling prefetch to see if prefetch-induced kv churn is the trigger.
Mira: and try adaptive_window reduce for long sessions to limit kv growth per request.
Taylor: I'll schedule a 2h soak with the new runtime and configs, then run a 500-prompt paired eval (int8 baseline vs int4 candidate) overnight. If int4 regression >1% we'll consider mixed fallback.
Ash: add alerts: OOM spike >1/min, p95 latency >1s, and a regression job to run post-soak.
infra-bot: soak job queued: soak-1839997777-1 owner=Taylor team=eng-ml
Kevin: note: quant packer bisects often show per-layer activation outliers. If soak still OOMs, I can start bisect on the quant packer and per-layer packing config.
Mira: followups assigned: Taylor=soak+eval, Kevin=runtime upgrade and packer bisect if needed, Ash=alerts+dashboards.
Taylor: kicking off soak in ~10m. Will post results in-thread.
Mira: thanks, this matches our quant-onboard frag playbook. Fingers crossed.
Taylor: posting results when available. :rocket:
